sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the denial itself] CENTCOM: 'All US military unmanned surface vessels in the Middle East are accounted for, including a squadron of advanced sea drones on patrol in the Strait of Hormuz supporting CENTCOM's defensive layer.' CENTCOM called the IRGC claim FALSE. [CONTESTED -- underlying incident] Iran's navy said Fri it struck and destroyed an 'enemy unmanned vessel' east of the strait (IRNA); it did not identify the vessel or operator. Neither side has produced wreckage or independent evidence, so whether any vessel was destroyed remains unresolved. sections.what_verified: CENTCOM X post itself (T1, OFFICIAL-PD) + Anadolu Agency relay (T3, STATE-TR) + Al Jazeera liveblog relay (T2, STATE-QA) = 3 distinct publisher families for the denial; TOI liveblog is an additional relay, not counted separately.
sections.what_disputed: Iran's navy claim stands unretracted (IRNA); no wreckage, imagery, or third-party verification from either side. CENTCOM's own 'accounted for' assertion is itself unverifiable from open sources. Do not present the denial as proof no vessel of any operator was hit -- Iran never named the US as operator in the original IRNA-carried statement; CENTCOM framed it as an IRGC claim about a US vessel.
sections.why_matters: Hormuz by the Numbers: claim vs denial in one evening -- Iran says it destroyed a US sea drone east of the Strait; CENTCOM answers 'all accounted for.' No wreckage, no proof, two statements.
